page: Microsoft Azure F48ads_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Fadsv7 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. This configuration delivers 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The hardware profile includes 192.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, featuring a 5669 GB NVMe SSD that is Premium Storage capable. The virtualization layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

In benchmark evaluations, the F48ads_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests, as well as Geekbench and Passmark CPU metrics. Memory bandwidth is highly competitive, with read-only small block cached operations and large block write operations scoring in the top 10%, while large block read-only bandwidth falls in the top 25%. The system excels in data processing tasks, achieving top-tier results in Redis SET operations, Passmark database operations, and bzip3 decompression. However, for large-scale machine learning workloads, the lack of a dedicated GPU results in a performance tradeoff; while LLM inference for small (135M) and medium (7B) models ranks in the top 10% to 25%, inference speeds for large (70B) models drop to the middle 50% average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F48ads_v7 offers high resource density by combining a high-frequency CPU with a substantial 5.6 TB local NVMe SSD. This eliminates the need for separate attached storage costs for high-throughput local operations. The instance is suited for database hosting, software compilation, web serving, and medium-scale text or image processing workloads. It is less optimal for heavy deep learning training or large-scale LLM execution due to the absence of hardware accelerators.
